PR9-F-01.hint: Find where the numerator is zero and where the denominator is zero. Both split the number line; test a point in each interval. A value that makes the denominator zero is never in the solution.
slips: Including the value that makes the denominator zero. It is always excluded, even for \(\le\) and \(\ge\).
Excluding the numerator's zero when the inequality includes equality.

PR9-A-01.hint: List every critical number: the zeros of the numerator and of the denominator. If the right side is not zero, move everything to one side and combine over a common denominator first.
slips: Multiplying both sides by the denominator. Its sign changes from interval to interval, so the direction of the inequality can change. Use a sign chart instead.
Forgetting one of the critical numbers, so one of the intervals is never tested.

parts.q: Solve \(\dfrac{- x + 6}{3 x + 7} \ge 0\). Express your answer in interval notation.
parts.a: The numerator is \(0\) at \(x = 6\) and the denominator is \(0\) at \(x = -\dfrac{7}{3}\). Use these two values to split the number line, then test a point in each interval. \(x = -\dfrac{7}{3}\) is never included because the expression is undefined there. \(x = 6\) is included because the inequality is not strict. Solution: \((-\dfrac{7}{3}, 6]\).

parts.q: Solve \(\dfrac{x - 1}{x - 4} \ge 0\). Express your answer in interval notation.

Use these two values to split the number line, then test a point in each interval. \(x = 4\) is never included because the expression is undefined there. \(x = 1\) is included because the inequality is not strict. Solution: \((-\infty, 1] \cup (4, \infty)\).
